rounds.proof_sketch: Mutation in maxpool1d_forward_kernel_batch_channel_parallel, invoked only when total_elements >= 65536. With input [16,64,128] and batch*channels=1024, need output_length>=64, requiring kernel_size<=2. Layer 2's 112 bitwise-equivalent rounds prove kernel_size>2 is used, so mutated kernel is never called.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation resides in maxpool1d_forward_kernel_batch_channel_parallel, which is only executed when total_elements >= 65536. With the fixed input shape [16, 64, 128] and fixed model parameters, the computation always takes the first branch (total_elements < 65536), invoking maxpool1d_forward_kernel instead. The 112 rounds of bitwise equivalence in Layer 2 testing confirm this - changing input tensor VALUES cannot affect which kernel is dispatched. The dispatch decision depends solely on output_length, which is determined by fixed model configuration parameters (kernel_size, stride, padding, dilation) that we cannot modify.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed configuration. Would require changing model parameters (kernel_size ≤ 2) to invoke the mutated kernel, which violates the testing contract.
rounds.recommendations: For mutation testing of kernels with problem-size-based dispatch, ensure the test suite includes configurations that exercise ALL code paths. Add explicit tests with kernel_size=1 or kernel_size=2 to reach maxpool1d_forward_kernel_batch_channel_parallel.
